The [Pomona room draw](https://www.pomona.edu/administration/housing-residence-life/housing-selection-and-processes) is a random assignment of a time, starting at 5:00pm and running one slot every 3 minutes with 4 students per slot, and with each class on a different day, for students to select their place of residence for the next school year. The most sought-after rooms (Sontag/Dialynas suites) go the quickest; however, students can group up with a friend and adopt the earlier time to get a better room. The question I hope to solve through this simulation is how the chances of getting a group time at or before 5:27pm (the most sought-after rooms on campus were all gone by 5:27pm for Fall 2025 housing) change as group size goes from 1 to 8 (note there are no groups of 7). I plan on simulating multiple random room draws and estimating the probability of each group size achieving a time at or before 5:27pm, because working it out by hand is quite difficult.
